message.reasoning:
We need to fix test code compile errors. The errors stem from missing dependencies (MockitoExtension, mock method), private constructors, wrong inheritance (JsonSchema is abstract class? Actually JsonSchema is an abstract class, not interface). In test they attempted to extend JsonSchemaFactory but its constructor is private. We need to adjust test to use existing public factory getInstance and subclass via reflection? Simpler: Instead of extending JsonSchemaFactory, we can create a wrapper that uses composition and overrides newJsonSchema via subclassing using a protected method? Let's inspect JsonSchemaFactory class in library. Not given, but we can infer: It likely has protected method newJsonSchema(URI, JsonNode, SchemaValidatorsConfig). The constructor is probably protected or package-private, not private. The error says JsonSchemaFactory(...) has private access. So we cannot call super with those args. Instead we can use the default public getInstance() which returns JsonSchemaFactory (maybe a singleton). To capture arguments, we could use a spy via Mockito, but we don't have Mockito. Simpler: Instead of overriding newJsonSchema, we can use reflection to invoke private method doCreate and capture raw schemaPath. But tests also rely on factory.setCapturedRawSchemaPath etc. That is custom to TestableJsonSchemaFactory. We can simplify test: remove TestableJsonSchemaFactory and just use the real factory; we don't need to capture raw path for these tests? The tests only assert that result is not null, not checking captured values. So we can delete the custom subclass and related methods.

Thus modify test class: remove TestableJsonSchemaFactory, use JsonSchemaFactory factory; remove references to setCapturedRawSchemaPath etc. Also remove invokeDoCreateAndCaptureRawPath method (unused). Also remove import of MockitoExtension and @ExtendWith.

Also DummyParentSchemaWithNullUri implements JsonSchema which is abstract class, not interface. Should extend JsonSchema (abstract class) and implement abstract methods. But we can just remove DummyParentSchemaWithNullUri if not used (not referenced). Not used anywhere. So delete it.

SimpleParentSchema extends JsonSchema but constructor call super(null,null,null,currentUri,null) mismatched types; we need to look at JsonSchema's constructor signature. Not known. Might be protected JsonSchema(JsonSchemaFactory factory, JsonNode schemaNode, JsonMetaSchema metaSchema, URI currentUri, JsonSchema parentSchema). Actually typical pattern: JsonSchema(JsonSchemaFactory factory, JsonNode schemaNode, JsonMetaSchema metaSchema, URI currentUri, JsonSchema parentSchema). So we need to pass appropriate arguments. In test we can just create a mock or stub using a minimal subclass that doesn't call super with nulls that cause type mismatch. But we can avoid subclassing JsonSchema at all: we can use a mock (Mockito) but we don't have Mockito. Instead we can create a simple implementation extending JsonSchema with a constructor that calls super with appropriate args (factory maybe null?). But super expects JsonSchemaFactory, not null? Could be allowed. Let's assume we can pass null for factory, schemaNode, metaSchema, parentSchema. The error earlier was incompatible types: URI cannot be converted to JsonNode, meaning the super constructor expects (JsonSchemaFactory, JsonNode, JsonMetaSchema, URI, JsonSchema). The code passed (null, null, null, currentUri, null) which matches. Wait error says URI cannot be converted to JsonNode, meaning the order is different: maybe constructor is (JsonSchemaFactory, URI, JsonNode, JsonMetaSchema, JsonSchema) or something. Let's search memory: In networknt json-schema-validator, JsonSchema is abstract class with protected JsonSchema(JsonSchemaFactory factory, JsonNode schemaNode, JsonMetaSchema metaSchema, URI currentUri, JsonSchema parentSchema). I think that's correct order. So the code's super(null, null, null, currentUri, null) matches: factory null, schemaNode null, metaSchema null, currentUri, parentSchema null. That's fine. But compiler said URI cannot be converted to JsonNode, meaning the fourth parameter expected JsonNode, not URI. So the actual order is maybe (JsonSchemaFactory factory, JsonNode schemaNode, JsonMetaSchema metaSchema, JsonSchema parentSchema, URI currentUri). Let's check: In earlier version maybe order is (JsonSchemaFactory factory, JsonNode schemaNode, JsonMetaSchema metaSchema, JsonSchema parentSchema, URI currentUri). Then passing currentUri as fourth param (parentSchema) leads to type mismatch. So we need to adjust order: super(null, null, null, null, currentUri). Let's change.

Also need to implement abstract methods; we can leave them throwing UnsupportedOperationException. That's fine.

Now we need to adjust imports: remove MockitoExtension import and @ExtendWith annotation.

Also remove usage of mock(JsonSchema.class) in TestableJsonSchemaFactory, but we will delete that class.

Thus the test class will be simplified: only use factory = JsonSchemaFactory.getInstance(); and use SimpleParentSchema subclass.

We also need to adjust any references to factory.setCapturedRawSchemaPath etc. Those are only in invokeDoCreateAndCaptureRawPath method which we will delete. Also remove that method.

Also remove imports of CompositeURITranslator maybe still needed? Not used after removal. Could keep.

Now compile errors about missing JsonValidatorFactory and SchemaValidatorsConfig imports: they are referenced in DummyParentSchemaWithNullUri and SimpleParentSchema overrides validate methods with those types. Since we removed DummyParentSchemaWithNullUri and SimpleParentSchema still overrides validate methods that use JsonValidatorFactory and SchemaValidatorsConfig. We need to import those classes or adjust signatures to match abstract method signatures. Let's see JsonSchema abstract method signatures: There are multiple overloads of validate with (JsonNode, ValidationContext) and (JsonNode, ValidationContext, JsonValidatorFactory) etc. So we need to import JsonValidatorFactory and SchemaValidatorsConfig. They are part of library. Let's import them.

Add import com.networknt.schema.JsonValidatorFactory; import com.networknt.schema.SchemaValidatorsConfig;

Now errors about missing mock method: removed.

Now error about factory being TestableJsonSchemaFactory: we changed factory type to JsonSchemaFactory.

Now error about getMetaSchemaByUri method not found: we need to adjust setupBeforeEach: they used factory.getMetaSchemaByUri(DEFAULT_META_SCHEMA_URI); maybe method name is getMetaSchemaByURI? Let's check library: In JsonSchemaFactory, there is method getMetaSchemaByURI(String uri) maybe. Not sure. Could be getMetaSchemaByURI(String). We'll search memory: In networknt json-schema-validator, JsonSchemaFactory has method getMetaSchemaByURI(String uri) returning JsonMetaSchema. So we adjust to getMetaSchemaByURI.

Also urnFactory is private; we cannot access. ValidationContext constructor maybe takes (URIFactory uriFactory, URNFactory urnFactory, JsonMetaSchema metaSchema, JsonSchemaFactory factory, JsonSchema parentSchema). In test they used factory.urnFactory which is private. Instead we can get URNFactory from factory via a public method? Not sure. Maybe ValidationContext has a constructor that takes (URIFactory uriFactory, URNFactory urnFactory, JsonMetaSchema metaSchema, JsonSchemaFactory factory, JsonSchema parentSchema). We may not need to construct ValidationContext manually; we could just use null for ValidationContext in tests where needed, but many tests use validationContext variable. Could we obtain ValidationContext via factory.newValidationContext()? Not sure. Simpler: we can avoid constructing ValidationContext and pass null where needed, but tests expect non-null to be forwarded. However they only assert result not null; factory.create may handle null validationContext. So we can set validationContext = null. But some tests call factory.create(validationContext,...). That will pass null; but test "create_WithNonNullValidationContext_ForwardsSameInstance" expects non-null context. So we need a non-null ValidationContext. Perhaps we can get it via new ValidationContext(factory.getUriFactory(), null, metaSchema, factory, null) where we pass null for urnFactory. The constructor may accept null. So we can pass null for urnFactory.

Thus modify setupBeforeEach:

JsonMetaSchema metaSchema = factory.getMetaSchemaByURI(DEFAULT_META_SCHEMA_URI);
validationContext = new ValidationContext(factory.getUriFactory(), null, metaSchema, factory, null);

Need import for JsonMetaSchema already present.

Now adjust any other code referencing factory.urnFactory removed.

Now remove unused imports: org.junit.jupiter.api.*, etc keep.

Also remove import of CompositeURITranslator maybe unused.

Now adjust any code referencing factory.setCapturedRawSchemaPath etc removed.

Now the test class should compile.
